# Gitleaks configuration for repos bootstrapped by agent-history-hygiene.
#
# Source of truth: ~/.local/share/chezmoi/.gitleaks.toml. This file is a
# portable subset copied in by `bootstrap-project.sh` for repos without
# chezmoi. Keep rule IDs stable so allowlists stay comparable.
#
# https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks#configuration

title = "agent-history-hygiene gitleaks config"

[extend]
useDefault = true

# Global allowlist: redaction sentinels + example-shape strings the agent
# legitimately discusses in transcripts/plans. Uses the [[allowlists]]
# array form (gitleaks v8 forbids mixing with the deprecated [allowlist]).
[[allowlists]]
  description = "Redaction sentinels + documentation-shape keys"
  regexTarget = "line"
  regexes = [
    # Already-redacted sentinels emitted by redact_secrets.py.
    '''\b[A-Za-z0-9_-]+_REDACTED(?:_[A-Z_]+)?\b''',
    # Truncated "sk-proj-XXX..." example shapes used in prose.
    '''sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{3,8}\.\.\.''',
  ]

# Path-scoped allowlist: inside agent artifact dirs, tolerate explicit
# example/demo markers without unlocking real leaks. Both the path AND a
# regex must match, so a real `sk-ant-api03-<95 chars>AA` still fires.
[[allowlists]]
  description = "Example/demo keys inside agent transcripts and plan files"
  # Both path and regex must match, otherwise any .md under these dirs
  # gets allowlisted wholesale (gitleaks v8 defaults to OR semantics).
  condition   = "AND"
  paths = [
    '''\.specstory/history/.*\.md$''',
    '''\.claude/plans/.*\.md$''',
    '''\.cursor/(plans|rules)/.*\.md$''',
    '''\.opencode/plans/.*\.md$''',
    '''\.specify/.*\.md$''',
    '''\.codex/.*\.md$''',
  ]
  regexTarget = "line"
  regexes = [
    '''example[-_]?(key|token|secret)''',
    '''\bREDACTED\b''',
    '''sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{3,8}\.\.\.''',
    '''your[-_]?(api[-_]?)?key[-_]?here''',
  ]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Custom rules -- prefix-anchored modern API keys gitleaks default rules miss
# or under-specify. Curated subset of the chezmoi config; rule IDs match so
# overrides in the user's chezmoi version remain compatible.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[rules]]
  id          = "openai-project-key"
  description = "OpenAI project-scoped API key (sk-proj-...)"
  regex       = '''\bsk-proj-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{80,}\b'''
  tags        = ["key", "openai", "auto"]

[[rules]]
  id          = "anthropic-api-key-strict"
  description = "Anthropic API key (sk-ant-apiNN-..., strict length)"
  regex       = '''\bsk-ant-api\d{2}-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{93}AA\b'''
  tags        = ["key", "anthropic", "auto"]

[[rules]]
  id          = "cursor-api-key"
  description = "Cursor API key (cursor- prefixed)"
  regex       = '''\bcursor-[A-Za-z0-9]{40,}\b'''
  tags        = ["key", "cursor", "auto"]

[[rules]]
  id          = "huggingface-token"
  description = "Hugging Face user access token (hf_...)"
  regex       = '''\bhf_[A-Za-z0-9]{34,40}\b'''
  tags        = ["key", "huggingface", "auto"]

[[rules]]
  id          = "supabase-service-pat"
  description = "Supabase service / personal access token (sbp_...)"
  regex       = '''\bsbp_[a-f0-9]{40}\b'''
  tags        = ["key", "supabase", "auto"]

[[rules]]
  id          = "linear-api-key"
  description = "Linear API key (lin_api_...)"
  regex       = '''\blin_api_[A-Za-z0-9]{40}\b'''
  tags        = ["key", "linear", "auto"]

[[rules]]
  id          = "tailscale-auth-key"
  description = "Tailscale auth/client/api key (tskey-...)"
  regex       = '''\btskey-(?:auth|client|api)-[A-Za-z0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9]{24,}\b'''
  tags        = ["key", "tailscale", "auto"]

[[rules]]
  id          = "notion-integration-token"
  description = "Notion internal integration token (ntn_...)"
  regex       = '''\bntn_[A-Za-z0-9]{40,}\b'''
  tags        = ["key", "notion", "auto"]

[[rules]]
  id          = "wakatime-api-key"
  description = "WakaTime API key (waka_ + RFC-4122 UUID)"
  regex       = '''\bwaka_[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}\b'''
  tags        = ["key", "wakatime", "auto"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Webhook URLs commonly emitted into LLM/agent transcripts during demos and
# test scaffolding. gitleaks default rules cover slack-webhook-url,
# microsoft-teams-webhook, and telegram-bot-api-token; these fill the gaps.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[rules]]
  id          = "discord-webhook-url"
  description = "Discord webhook URL (discord.com / discordapp.com / ptb / canary)"
  regex       = '''https?://(?:(?:ptb|canary)\.)?discord(?:app)?\.com/api/webhooks/\d{17,20}/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{60,80}'''
  tags        = ["webhook", "discord", "auto"]

[[rules]]
  id          = "zapier-webhook-url"
  description = "Zapier catch hook URL (hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/...)"
  regex       = '''https?://hooks\.zapier\.com/hooks/catch/\d{6,12}/[A-Za-z0-9]{5,}/?'''
  tags        = ["webhook", "zapier", "auto"]

[[rules]]
  id          = "make-webhook-url"
  description = "Make.com / Integromat webhook URL"
  regex       = '''https?://hook\.(?:[a-z]{2}\d+\.make\.com|integromat\.com)/[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}'''
  tags        = ["webhook", "make", "integromat", "auto"]

[[rules]]
  id          = "stripe-webhook-secret"
  description = "Stripe webhook signing secret (whsec_...)"
  regex       = '''\bwhsec_[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}\b'''
  tags        = ["webhook", "stripe", "auto"]

"""Shared pytest fixtures for the agent-history-hygiene test suite.

The redactor under test (`assets/redact_secrets.py`) is a PEP 723 uv
script with a `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script` shebang. Its body is
otherwise a plain Python module — we load it via `importlib` so tests
can call individual functions without shelling out.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

SKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
ASSETS_DIR = SKILL_ROOT / "assets"
SCRIPTS_DIR = SKILL_ROOT / "scripts"
FIXTURES_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures"


def _load_redact_secrets_module():
    """Import assets/redact_secrets.py as a module despite the shebang."""
    script_path = ASSETS_DIR / "redact_secrets.py"
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("redact_secrets", script_path)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:  # pragma: no cover — defensive
        raise RuntimeError(f"Could not load spec for {script_path}")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules["redact_secrets"] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def redact_secrets():
    """The imported redact_secrets module."""
    return _load_redact_secrets_module()


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def fixtures_dir() -> Path:
    """Directory containing *.md corpus files."""
    return FIXTURES_DIR


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def assets_dir() -> Path:
    """Skill-local assets/ (templates + bundled redactor)."""
    return ASSETS_DIR


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def scripts_dir() -> Path:
    """Skill-local scripts/."""
    return SCRIPTS_DIR


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def gitleaks_available() -> bool:
    """Whether the gitleaks CLI is on PATH. Corpus tests skip when false."""
    return shutil.which("gitleaks") is not None


@pytest.fixture
def tmp_git_repo(tmp_path: Path, assets_dir: Path):
    """Bootstrap an empty git repo in tmp_path with our .gitleaks.toml
    config copied in. Returns the repo path.

    Uses -c user.email/name so the test works on CI boxes without a
    configured git identity.
    """
    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
    repo.mkdir()
    subprocess.run(
        ["git", "init", "-q", "-b", "main"],
        cwd=repo,
        check=True,
    )
    # Copy our gitleaks config so rules + allowlists apply.
    shutil.copy(assets_dir / "gitleaks.toml.template", repo / ".gitleaks.toml")
    # Seed an initial commit so --staged has something to diff against.
    (repo / "README.md").write_text("init\n", encoding="utf-8")
    subprocess.run(
        [
            "git",
            "-c",
            "user.email=test@example.com",
            "-c",
            "user.name=test",
            "commit",
            "-q",
            "--allow-empty",
            "-m",
            "init",
        ],
        cwd=repo,
        check=True,
    )
    return repo
===== tests/README =====
# Tests for agent-history-hygiene

Run the full suite:

```bash
# From repo root
make test-skill

# Or directly
uv run --extra dev pytest skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/tests/ -q
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/tests/test_scan_staged.sh
```

## Layout

- `fixtures/` — paired `.md` files exercising gitleaks rules + allowlist.
  Each filename encodes its expected behavior (e.g. `real_anthropic.md`
  should fire, `example_shapes.md` should be allowlisted when staged
  inside an agent-artifact directory).
- `conftest.py` — shared pytest fixtures; loads the PEP 723 script
  `assets/redact_secrets.py` as an importable module.
- `test_redact_secrets.py` — unit tests for pure functions in the
  redactor (`redact_secret`, `filter_by_prefixes`,
  `find_private_key_files`, `redact_file`, `redact_private_keys`).
- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus tests: stages each fixture
  in a throwaway git repo and asserts `gitleaks git --staged` returns
  the expected findings (or lack thereof). Skipped if `gitleaks` is
  not on `PATH`.
- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
  `scripts/scan-staged.sh`: `0` clean, `20` leak, `30` missing
  gitleaks, `2` not a git repo.

## Why these three levels

The skill already surfaced three regressions during initial hand
verification — each one would have been caught here:

| Regression                                                  | Caught by                |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| Allowlist defaulted to `OR` between paths + regex           | `test_gitleaks_corpus`   |
| `[allowlist]` singular clashed with `[[allowlists]]` plural | `test_gitleaks_corpus`   |
| `gitleaks dir` silently skipped hidden paths                | `test_redact_secrets`    |
| JSON report `[]` treated as "leaks found"                   | `test_scan_staged.sh`    |

## Requirements

- `uv` (for `uv run --extra dev pytest`)
- `gitleaks` on `PATH` (corpus tests + shell test skip gracefully when
  missing — the pytest file xfails with a clear message, the shell
  test exits 0 for the "no gitleaks" case)
- `git` configured with a user identity (the shell test uses
  `-c user.email=...`)

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scan-staged.sh — run gitleaks on the current staged diff with
3	# agent-friendly exit codes.
4	#
5	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
6	
7	set -euo pipefail
8	
9	usage() {
10	  cat <<'EOF'
11	Usage: scan-staged.sh [OPTIONS]
12	
13	Scan the staged diff for secrets using `gitleaks git --staged`. Intended
14	as the "last line of defense" wrapper agents call before `git commit` so
15	they can branch on structured exit codes.
16	
17	Options:
18	  --redact           Pass --redact to gitleaks (default: off; findings
19	                     print the literal secret for debugging).
20	  --no-redact        Explicit opt-out of --redact (overrides --redact).
21	  --config PATH      Path to .gitleaks.toml (default: repo root if present).
22	  --verbose          Print gitleaks' own output to stderr.
23	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
24	
25	Output (stdout):
26	  - If clean: no output.
27	  - If leaks found: one JSON object per line with the finding details.
28	
29	Exit codes:
30	  0   clean — no secrets found
31	  10  leaks found (and redacted if --redact was passed)
32	  20  leaks found, not redacted (caller must rotate + re-stage)
33	  30  gitleaks binary not installed
34	  40  gitleaks error (bad config, unreadable repo, etc.)
35	  1   invalid arguments
36	  2   not inside a git repo
37	EOF
38	}
39	
40	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
41	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
42	
43	REDACT=0
44	CONFIG=""
45	VERBOSE=0
46	
47	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
48	  case "$1" in
49	    --redact)     REDACT=1; shift ;;
50	    --no-redact)  REDACT=0; shift ;;
51	    --config)     CONFIG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
52	    --config=*)   CONFIG="${1#--config=}"; shift ;;
53	    --verbose)    VERBOSE=1; shift ;;
54	    --help|-h)    usage; exit 0 ;;
55	    -*)           die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
56	    *)            die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
57	  esac
58	done
59	
60	# Check prerequisites.
61	if ! command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
62	  log "gitleaks not installed. Install hints:"
63	  log "  macOS:   brew install gitleaks"
64	  log "  Linux:   https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases"
65	  exit 30
66	fi
67	
68	if ! git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
69	  die "not inside a git repo" 2
70	fi
71	cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
72	
73	# Auto-discover config if not specified.
74	if [ -z "$CONFIG" ] && [ -f ".gitleaks.toml" ]; then
75	  CONFIG=".gitleaks.toml"
76	fi
77	
78	report_path="$(mktemp -t gitleaks-report.XXXXXX.json)"
79	trap 'rm -f "$report_path"' EXIT
80	
81	# Assemble the command. Post v8.19.0 `gitleaks git --staged` replaces the
82	# deprecated `gitleaks protect --staged`.
83	cmd=(gitleaks git --staged
84	     --report-format json
85	     --report-path "$report_path"
86	     --exit-code 0)
87	[ -n "$CONFIG" ] && cmd+=(--config "$CONFIG")
88	[ "$REDACT" = "1" ] && cmd+=(--redact)
89	
90	# Capture gitleaks' own exit code — with `--exit-code 0` it returns 0
91	# whether leaks are found or not, so a non-zero exit means the tool itself
92	# failed (config error, unreadable repo, etc.).
93	stderr_capture="$(mktemp -t gitleaks-stderr.XXXXXX)"
94	trap 'rm -f "$report_path" "$stderr_capture"' EXIT
95	
96	gl_rc=0
97	if [ "$VERBOSE" = "1" ]; then
98	  "${cmd[@]}" >&2 2>>"$stderr_capture" || gl_rc=$?
99	else
100	  "${cmd[@]}" >/dev/null 2>"$stderr_capture" || gl_rc=$?
101	fi
102	
103	if [ "$gl_rc" -ne 0 ]; then
104	  log "gitleaks failed to run (exit $gl_rc). Tail of its stderr:"
105	  tail -n 20 "$stderr_capture" >&2 || true
106	  exit 40
107	fi
108	
109	# Gitleaks writes an empty file when truly clean, or `[]` when the report
110	# format is JSON and there are zero findings. Normalize both to "clean".
111	if [ ! -s "$report_path" ]; then
112	  exit 0
113	fi
114	
115	finding_count=0
116	if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
117	  finding_count=$(python3 - "$report_path" <<'PY'
118	import json, sys
119	try:
120	    with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as f:
121	        data = json.load(f)
122	except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
123	    print(0)
124	    sys.exit(0)
125	print(len(data) if isinstance(data, list) else 0)
126	PY
127	)
128	else
129	  # Fallback: grep for a non-empty array. `[]` → 0, anything else → non-zero.
130	  case "$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$report_path")" in
131	    ""|"[]") finding_count=0 ;;
132	    *)        finding_count=1 ;;
133	  esac
134	fi
135	
136	if [ "$finding_count" -eq 0 ]; then
137	  exit 0
138	fi
139	
140	# Re-emit each finding as its own JSON object (one per line) for ergonomic
141	# agent consumption. Findings file is a JSON *array*; slice it into lines
142	# using python3 — avoid adding a jq dependency.
143	if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
144	  python3 - "$report_path" <<'PY'
145	import json, sys
146	with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as f:
147	    data = json.load(f)
148	for finding in data:
149	    # Keep only the most useful fields; caller can re-open the raw report.
150	    slim = {
151	        "rule_id": finding.get("RuleID"),
152	        "file": finding.get("File"),
153	        "line": finding.get("StartLine"),
154	        "commit": finding.get("Commit") or "STAGED",
155	        "match": finding.get("Match"),
156	    }
157	    print(json.dumps(slim, ensure_ascii=False))
158	PY
159	else
160	  # Fallback: dump the raw array.
161	  cat "$report_path"
162	fi
163	
164	if [ "$REDACT" = "1" ]; then
165	  log "gitleaks found leaks AND --redact was passed."
166	  log "  NOTE: gitleaks --redact only masks the CLI output, it does NOT"
167	  log "        rewrite files. Use redact_secrets.py --fix (or the pre-commit"
168	  log "        redact-agent-secrets hook) to actually scrub the artifacts."
169	  exit 10
170	else
171	  log "gitleaks found leaks. See JSON findings on stdout."
172	  log "Next: rotate the secret at the provider, then run redact_secrets.py --fix,"
173	  log "      then re-stage and re-run this check. DO NOT \`git push --force\`."
174	  exit 20
175	fi
176
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# stage-agent-artifacts.sh — git-add agent chat + plan artifacts before
3	# the next commit.
4	#
5	# Default behavior: stage every dirty *.md under each directory in
6	# assets/artifact-dirs.txt, plus the current SpecStory transcript.
7	#
8	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
9	
10	set -euo pipefail
11	
12	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
13	SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
14	DEFAULT_DIRS_FILE="$SKILL_DIR/assets/artifact-dirs.txt"
15	
16	usage() {
17	  cat <<'EOF'
18	Usage: stage-agent-artifacts.sh [OPTIONS]
19	
20	Stage agent artifact files (SpecStory transcripts, .claude/plans/*.md, etc.)
21	for the next commit. Must be run from inside a git repo.
22	
23	Options:
24	  --session-only        Only stage the current SpecStory transcript + newest
25	                        plan file; skip .cursor/, .opencode/, etc.
26	  --include-all-plans   Also re-add already-tracked plan/transcript files
27	                        that were modified (default: only unstaged files).
28	  --dirs-file PATH      Override the default artifact-dirs.txt location.
29	  --dry-run             Print the files that would be staged, but don't stage.
30	  --allow-empty         Stage artifacts even when HEAD has no code changes
31	                        (default: refuse — prevents "commit just transcript").
32	  --help, -h            Show this help and exit.
33	
34	Exit codes:
35	  0  success (one or more artifacts staged or already clean)
36	  1  invalid arguments
37	  2  not inside a git repo
38	  3  no code changes AND no dirty artifacts (suggests nothing to commit)
39	  4  refused: code is clean but artifacts are dirty (use --allow-empty)
40	EOF
41	}
42	
43	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
44	warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
45	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
46	
47	SESSION_ONLY=0
48	INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS=0
49	DIRS_FILE="$DEFAULT_DIRS_FILE"
50	DRY_RUN=0
51	ALLOW_EMPTY=0
52	
53	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
54	  case "$1" in
55	    --session-only)       SESSION_ONLY=1; shift ;;
56	    --include-all-plans)  INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS=1; shift ;;
57	    --dirs-file)          DIRS_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
58	    --dirs-file=*)        DIRS_FILE="${1#--dirs-file=}"; shift ;;
59	    --dry-run)            DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
60	    --allow-empty)        ALLOW_EMPTY=1; shift ;;
61	    --help|-h)            usage; exit 0 ;;
62	    -*)                   die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
63	    *)                    die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
64	  esac
65	done
66	
67	# Must be in a git repo.
68	if ! git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
69	  die "not inside a git repo" 2
70	fi
71	REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
72	cd "$REPO_ROOT"
73	
74	# Read artifact dirs from the config file.
75	if [ ! -f "$DIRS_FILE" ]; then
76	  die "artifact-dirs.txt not found: $DIRS_FILE" 1
77	fi
78	
79	ARTIFACT_DIRS=()
80	while IFS= read -r line; do
81	  # Strip comments and whitespace.
82	  line="${line%%#*}"
83	  line="$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')"
84	  [ -n "$line" ] && ARTIFACT_DIRS+=("$line")
85	done < "$DIRS_FILE"
86	
87	# Warn if any artifact dir is silently gitignored.
88	check_ignored() {
89	  local dir="$1"
90	  # `git check-ignore` exits 0 if the path matches an ignore rule.
91	  if [ -e "$dir" ] && git check-ignore -q "$dir" 2>/dev/null; then
92	    warn "$dir is gitignored — staged files under it won't actually be committed"
93	  fi
94	}
95	
96	# Resolve the "current session" artifacts for --session-only.
97	find_current_specstory() {
98	  "$SCRIPT_DIR/find-session.sh" --quiet --format=specstory 2>/dev/null \
99	    | awk -F'\t' '$1=="specstory_path"{print $2}'
100	}
101	find_current_plan() {
102	  [ -d ".claude/plans" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
103	  find .claude/plans -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.md' -print0 2>/dev/null \
104	    | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null | head -n 1
105	}
106	
107	# List dirty artifact files across the configured dirs.
108	# Returns null-separated paths on stdout.
109	list_dirty_artifacts() {
110	  local dir path git_status
111	  for dir in "${ARTIFACT_DIRS[@]}"; do
112	    [ -e "$dir" ] || continue
113	    check_ignored "$dir"
114	    # Include untracked (??) and modified (M/A) entries. `-z` → NUL separated.
115	    while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
116	      # porcelain -z format: XY<space>path[\0orig_path]
117	      # We only want the path portion.
118	      git_status="${entry:0:2}"
119	      path="${entry:3}"
120	      case "$path" in
121	        *.md) ;;
122	        *) continue ;;
123	      esac
124	      case "$git_status" in
125	        "??") printf '%s\0' "$path" ;;
126	        " M"|"MM"|"AM"|"AD"|"A ") printf '%s\0' "$path" ;;
127	        "M "|"A ")
128	          # Already staged — only re-add if --include-all-plans.
129	          [ "$INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS" = "1" ] && printf '%s\0' "$path"
130	          ;;
131	      esac
132	    done < <(git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall -- "$dir" 2>/dev/null || true)
133	  done
134	}
135	
136	# --- Main ---
137	STAGED_COUNT=0
138	CANDIDATES=()
139	
140	if [ "$SESSION_ONLY" = "1" ]; then
141	  specstory=$(find_current_specstory)
142	  plan=$(find_current_plan)
143	  [ -n "$specstory" ] && [ -f "$specstory" ] && CANDIDATES+=("$specstory")
144	  [ -n "$plan" ] && [ -f "$plan" ] && CANDIDATES+=("$plan")
145	else
146	  # Capture the dirty artifact list.
147	  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
148	    CANDIDATES+=("$f")
149	  done < <(list_dirty_artifacts)
150	fi
151	
152	# Check: are there code changes outside the artifact dirs?
153	# Non-artifact dirty files (staged or unstaged) mean the agent is committing
154	# a real feature alongside the transcript — that's the intended use.
155	has_code_changes() {
156	  local any=0 line path in_artifact dir
157	  while IFS= read -r line; do
158	    [ -z "$line" ] && continue
159	    path="${line:3}"
160	    in_artifact=0
161	    for dir in "${ARTIFACT_DIRS[@]}"; do
162	      case "$path" in
163	        "$dir"/*) in_artifact=1; break ;;
164	      esac
165	    done
166	    [ "$in_artifact" = "0" ] && any=1
167	  done < <(git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain=v1 2>/dev/null)
168	  [ "$any" = "1" ]
169	}
170	
171	if [ "${#CANDIDATES[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
172	  if has_code_changes; then
173	    log "No agent artifacts to stage; code changes present — nothing to do."
174	    exit 0
175	  fi
176	  log "Nothing to stage: no code changes and no dirty artifacts."
177	  exit 3
178	fi
179	
180	if [ "$ALLOW_EMPTY" = "0" ] && ! has_code_changes; then
181	  log "Refusing: artifacts are dirty but no code changes staged."
182	  log "         A transcript/plan commit without a feature diff is usually wrong."
183	  log "         Re-run with --allow-empty if you really want to commit artifacts alone."
184	  exit 4
185	fi
186	
187	# Stage (or print).
188	for f in "${CANDIDATES[@]}"; do
189	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
190	    printf '[dry-run] would git add: %s\n' "$f"
191	  else
192	    git add -- "$f"
193	    printf 'staged: %s\n' "$f"
194	  fi
195	  STAGED_COUNT=$((STAGED_COUNT + 1))
196	done
197	
198	log "${STAGED_COUNT} artifact(s) ${DRY_RUN:+would be }staged."

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# test_scan_staged.sh — exit-code contract for scripts/scan-staged.sh.
3	#
4	# Asserts the documented exit codes:
5	#   0   clean
6	#   20  leaks found
7	#   30  gitleaks binary missing
8	#    2  not inside a git repo
9	#
10	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
11	
12	set -u  # intentionally NOT -e: we capture non-zero exit codes
13	
14	TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
15	SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/.." && pwd)"
16	SCAN="$SKILL_DIR/scripts/scan-staged.sh"
17	FIXTURES="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures"
18	
19	# State (no associative arrays — bash 3.2 compat)
20	PASS_COUNT=0
21	FAIL_COUNT=0
22	FAIL_LOG=""
23	
24	red()   { printf '\033[31m%s\033[0m' "$*"; }
25	green() { printf '\033[32m%s\033[0m' "$*"; }
26	dim()   { printf '\033[2m%s\033[0m' "$*"; }
27	
28	pass() {
29	  PASS_COUNT=$((PASS_COUNT + 1))
30	  printf '  %s %s\n' "$(green PASS)" "$1"
31	}
32	fail() {
33	  FAIL_COUNT=$((FAIL_COUNT + 1))
34	  printf '  %s %s\n' "$(red FAIL)" "$1"
35	  FAIL_LOG="${FAIL_LOG}FAIL: $1\n"
36	}
37	
38	# make_repo — spin up an isolated tmp repo with an initial commit.
39	# Prints the path to stdout.
40	make_repo() {
41	  local d
42	  d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/test-scan-staged.XXXXXX)
43	  git -C "$d" init -q -b main
44	  git -C "$d" -c user.email=test@example.com -c user.name=test \
45	      commit -q --allow-empty -m init
46	  printf '%s' "$d"
47	}
48	
49	# Copy fixture + stage it under the given relative path.

=== scan-staged.sh ===
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# scan-staged.sh — run gitleaks on the current staged diff with
     3	# agent-friendly exit codes.
     4	#
     5	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
     6	
     7	set -euo pipefail
     8	
     9	usage() {
    10	  cat <<'EOF'
    11	Usage: scan-staged.sh [OPTIONS]
    12	
    13	Scan the staged diff for secrets using `gitleaks git --staged`. Intended
    14	as the "last line of defense" wrapper agents call before `git commit` so
    15	they can branch on structured exit codes.
    16	
    17	Options:
    18	  --redact           Pass --redact to gitleaks (default: off; findings
    19	                     print the literal secret for debugging).
    20	  --no-redact        Explicit opt-out of --redact (overrides --redact).
    21	  --config PATH      Path to .gitleaks.toml (default: repo root if present).
    22	  --verbose          Print gitleaks' own output to stderr.
    23	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
    24	
    25	Output (stdout):
    26	  - If clean: no output.
    27	  - If leaks found: one JSON object per line with the finding details.
    28	
    29	Exit codes:
    30	  0   clean — no secrets found
    31	  10  leaks found (and redacted if --redact was passed)
    32	  20  leaks found, not redacted (caller must rotate + re-stage)
    33	  30  gitleaks binary not installed
    34	  40  gitleaks error (bad config, unreadable repo, etc.)
    35	  1   invalid arguments
    36	  2   not inside a git repo
    37	EOF
    38	}
    39	
    40	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
    41	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
    42	
    43	REDACT=0
    44	CONFIG=""
    45	VERBOSE=0
    46	
    47	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    48	  case "$1" in
    49	    --redact)     REDACT=1; shift ;;
    50	    --no-redact)  REDACT=0; shift ;;
    51	    --config)     CONFIG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    52	    --config=*)   CONFIG="${1#--config=}"; shift ;;
    53	    --verbose)    VERBOSE=1; shift ;;
    54	    --help|-h)    usage; exit 0 ;;
    55	    -*)           die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
    56	    *)            die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
    57	  esac
    58	done
    59	
    60	# Check prerequisites.
    61	if ! command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    62	  log "gitleaks not installed. Install hints:"
    63	  log "  macOS:   brew install gitleaks"
    64	  log "  Linux:   https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases"
    65	  exit 30
    66	fi
    67	
    68	if ! git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    69	  die "not inside a git repo" 2
    70	fi
    71	cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
    72	
    73	# Auto-discover config if not specified.
    74	if [ -z "$CONFIG" ] && [ -f ".gitleaks.toml" ]; then
    75	  CONFIG=".gitleaks.toml"
    76	fi
    77	
    78	report_path="$(mktemp -t gitleaks-report.XXXXXX.json)"
    79	trap 'rm -f "$report_path"' EXIT
    80	
    81	# Assemble the command. Post v8.19.0 `gitleaks git --staged` replaces the
    82	# deprecated `gitleaks protect --staged`.
    83	cmd=(gitleaks git --staged
    84	     --report-format json
    85	     --report-path "$report_path"
    86	     --exit-code 0)
    87	[ -n "$CONFIG" ] && cmd+=(--config "$CONFIG")
    88	[ "$REDACT" = "1" ] && cmd+=(--redact)
    89	
    90	# Capture gitleaks' own exit code — with `--exit-code 0` it returns 0
    91	# whether leaks are found or not, so a non-zero exit means the tool itself
    92	# failed (config error, unreadable repo, etc.).
    93	stderr_capture="$(mktemp -t gitleaks-stderr.XXXXXX)"
    94	trap 'rm -f "$report_path" "$stderr_capture"' EXIT
    95	
    96	gl_rc=0
    97	if [ "$VERBOSE" = "1" ]; then
    98	  "${cmd[@]}" >&2 2>>"$stderr_capture" || gl_rc=$?
    99	else
   100	  "${cmd[@]}" >/dev/null 2>"$stderr_capture" || gl_rc=$?
   101	fi
   102	
   103	if [ "$gl_rc" -ne 0 ]; then
   104	  log "gitleaks failed to run (exit $gl_rc). Tail of its stderr:"
   105	  tail -n 20 "$stderr_capture" >&2 || true
   106	  exit 40
   107	fi
   108	
   109	# Gitleaks writes an empty file when truly clean, or `[]` when the report
   110	# format is JSON and there are zero findings. Normalize both to "clean".
   111	if [ ! -s "$report_path" ]; then
   112	  exit 0
   113	fi
   114	
   115	finding_count=0
   116	if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   117	  finding_count=$(python3 - "$report_path" <<'PY'
   118	import json, sys
   119	try:
   120	    with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as f:
   121	        data = json.load(f)
   122	except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
   123	    print(0)
   124	    sys.exit(0)
   125	print(len(data) if isinstance(data, list) else 0)
   126	PY
   127	)
   128	else
   129	  # Fallback: grep for a non-empty array. `[]` → 0, anything else → non-zero.
   130	  case "$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$report_path")" in
   131	    ""|"[]") finding_count=0 ;;
   132	    *)        finding_count=1 ;;
   133	  esac
   134	fi
   135	
   136	if [ "$finding_count" -eq 0 ]; then
   137	  exit 0
   138	fi
   139	
   140	# Re-emit each finding as its own JSON object (one per line) for ergonomic
   141	# agent consumption. Findings file is a JSON *array*; slice it into lines
   142	# using python3 — avoid adding a jq dependency.
   143	if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   144	  python3 - "$report_path" <<'PY'
   145	import json, sys
   146	with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as f:
   147	    data = json.load(f)
   148	for finding in data:
   149	    # Keep only the most useful fields; caller can re-open the raw report.
   150	    slim = {
   151	        "rule_id": finding.get("RuleID"),
   152	        "file": finding.get("File"),
   153	        "line": finding.get("StartLine"),
   154	        "commit": finding.get("Commit") or "STAGED",
   155	        "match": finding.get("Match"),
   156	    }
   157	    print(json.dumps(slim, ensure_ascii=False))
   158	PY
   159	else
   160	  # Fallback: dump the raw array.
   161	  cat "$report_path"
   162	fi
   163	
   164	if [ "$REDACT" = "1" ]; then
   165	  log "gitleaks found leaks AND --redact was passed."
   166	  log "  NOTE: gitleaks --redact only masks the CLI output, it does NOT"
   167	  log "        rewrite files. Use redact_secrets.py --fix (or the pre-commit"
   168	  log "        redact-agent-secrets hook) to actually scrub the artifacts."
   169	  exit 10
   170	else
   171	  log "gitleaks found leaks. See JSON findings on stdout."
   172	  log "Next: rotate the secret at the provider, then run redact_secrets.py --fix,"
   173	  log "      then re-stage and re-run this check. DO NOT \`git push --force\`."
   174	  exit 20
   175	fi

     1	# Pre-commit hooks for a project bootstrapped by agent-history-hygiene.
     2	#
     3	# Installed by `bootstrap-project.sh`. The `files:` regex is rendered from

    13	  # Auto-redact leaked secrets in agent artifacts BEFORE gitleaks runs.
    14	  # If a file is rewritten pre-commit surfaces "files were modified by this
    15	  # hook" and the user must `git add` + recommit -- same UX as
    16	  # trailing-whitespace or end-of-file-fixer.
    17	  - repo: local
    18	    hooks:

    20	        name: Auto-redact secrets in agent artifacts

    24	        # {{BOOTSTRAP_RENDER: files_regex}} -- rendered from artifact-dirs.txt

    27	  # Gitleaks -- block commit when unallowlisted secrets are detected.
    28	  - repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
    29	    rev: v8.22.1
    30	    hooks:
    31	      # Prefer system-installed gitleaks to avoid Go toolchain build issues.

```text
=== pre-commit-redaction-stack.md ===
     1	# Pre-commit redaction stack
     2	
     3	The three-layer defense agents can rely on when committing agent
     4	transcripts + plan files.
     5	
     6	```
     7	  staged .md (transcript / plan)
     8	            │
     9	            ▼
    10	  Layer 1: redact-agent-secrets   (pre-commit, local hook)
    11	            │  rewrites file in place, re-stages via pre-commit
    12	            ▼
    13	  Layer 2: gitleaks-system         (pre-commit, github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks)
    14	            │  blocks commit if a rule still matches
    15	            ▼
    16	  Layer 3: scan-staged.sh          (agent-invoked, belt-and-suspenders)
    17	            │  run by the agent before `git commit` to branch on exit codes
    18	            ▼
    19	         git commit
    20	```
    21	
    22	Layers 1 and 2 are installed by `bootstrap-project.sh`. Layer 3 is the
    23	wrapper agents are expected to call before committing so they can react
    24	to structured exit codes without parsing pre-commit output.
    25	
    26	## Layer 1: redact-agent-secrets
    27	
    28	Implemented by `assets/redact_secrets.py`, wired as a `local` pre-commit
    29	hook in `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template`. On each commit:
    30	
    31	1. Pre-commit matches staged files against the `files:` regex
    32	   (rendered from `assets/artifact-dirs.txt`).
    33	2. `redact_secrets.py --fix` runs gitleaks against those files in staged
    34	   mode, gathers findings, and replaces each literal secret with
    35	   `first3...last3` (e.g. `sk-proj-abc...xyz`).
    36	3. Private-key PEM blocks (`-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----`) are
    37	   replaced wholesale with `[REDACTED PRIVATE KEY BLOCK]`, and the
    38	   literal string `PRIVATE KEY` becomes `PRIV***KEY` to stop the
    39	   detect-private-key hook from firing downstream.
    40	4. Any modified file is rewritten on disk. Pre-commit notices and exits
    41	   non-zero with "files were modified by this hook" — the user then
    42	   `git add`s the redacted files and recommits. Same UX as
    43	   trailing-whitespace or end-of-file-fixer.
    44	
    45	### Why redact (Layer 1) instead of block (Layer 2) for agent artifacts?
    46	
    47	Because "blocking" a chat transcript on a leak is useless — the secret
    48	is already in the file system, in the shell history, in the agent's
    49	conversation context. The only defense left is "don't let it hit
    50	`origin/`". Rewriting the file is the cheapest way to achieve that
    51	while keeping the surrounding prose intact for future readers.
    52	
    53	## Layer 2: gitleaks-system
    54	
    55	The upstream `github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks` hook (pinned at `v8.22.1` in
    56	the template). Runs after Layer 1 so it sees the redacted file. With
    57	`.gitleaks.toml` in the repo root, custom rules apply automatically.
    58	
    59	### Allowlist design
    60	
    61	Two allowlists in `gitleaks.toml.template`:
    62	
    63	- **Global** (`[allowlist]`): tolerates `*_REDACTED*` sentinels emitted
    64	  by Layer 1, plus truncated example shapes like `sk-proj-abc...`.
    65	- **Path-scoped** (`[[allowlists]]` with `paths`): inside agent
    66	  artifact directories, tolerate example markers (`example-key`,
    67	  `your-api-key-here`) and truncated example shapes. Both the **path
    68	  AND a regex** must match — a real `sk-ant-api03-<95 chars>AA` inside
    69	  a transcript still fires.
    70	
    71	Real leaks take precedence over documentation because gitleaks evaluates
    72	the finding's actual bytes, and truncated-example shapes don't have
    73	enough entropy to match the strict rules in the first place.
    74	
    75	## Layer 3: scan-staged.sh
    76	
    77	Belt-and-suspenders wrapper:
    78	
    79	```bash
    80	bash /path/to/skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh
    81	```
    82	
    83	Runs `gitleaks git --staged` and translates the outcome into exit codes
    84	agents can branch on:
    85	
    86	| Exit | Meaning                              | Typical agent reaction                                  |
    87	|-----:|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
    88	|    0 | Clean                                | Proceed with `git commit`                               |
    89	|   10 | Leaks found, `--redact` passed       | Run `redact_secrets.py --fix`, re-stage, re-run         |
    90	|   20 | Leaks found, no redaction            | Rotate secret at provider, then redact + re-stage       |
    91	|   30 | gitleaks not installed               | Surface install hint; fall back to bare pre-commit      |
    92	|    2 | Not inside a git repo                | Abort or bootstrap a repo first                         |
    93	
    94	Scripts always emit **JSON-lines findings on stdout** so the agent can
    95	feed them to follow-up tooling without parsing prose.
    96	
    97	## Keeping the bundled redactor in sync with chezmoi
    98	
    99	The chezmoi version at `~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/redact_secrets.py`
   100	is the **upstream source of truth**. The skill bundles a copy under
   101	`assets/redact_secrets.py` so non-chezmoi users still get protection.
   102	
   103	When chezmoi ships a fix, re-sync:
   104	
   105	```bash
   106	cp ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/redact_secrets.py \
   107	   $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/assets/redact_secrets.py
   108	git diff -- skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/assets/redact_secrets.py
   109	# review, adjust DEFAULT_PATHS if the skill's list differs, commit.
   110	```
   111	
   112	The skill's copy intentionally widens `DEFAULT_PATHS` beyond chezmoi's
   113	default (adds `.cursor/rules`, `.specify`, `.codex`). If chezmoi later
   114	adopts the wider list, the two converge; otherwise keep the skill
   115	version as the broader superset.
   116	
   117	## Inline allowlist pragmas
   118	
   119	For one-off false positives that don't deserve a config change, gitleaks
   120	accepts inline `#gitleaks:allow` on the same line as the match. Use
   121	sparingly — every pragma is an opportunity for a real secret to ride
   122	along in review.
   123	
   124	```
   125	# Example call pattern:
   126	# curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-proj-fake1234..." #gitleaks:allow
   127	```
   128	
   129	For whole-file exceptions, prefer adding a path to `.gitleaksignore`
   130	(one glob per line, gitignore syntax).
   131	
   132	## Cross-reference
   133	
   134	- [`transcript-session-discovery.md`](./transcript-session-discovery.md)
   135	  — how we locate which files to scan.
   136	- [`remediation.md`](./remediation.md) — what to do when Layer 3 fires
   137	  on an already-pushed commit.
   138	- [`../assets/artifact-dirs.txt`](../assets/artifact-dirs.txt) — the
   139	  shared source of truth for "which directories contain agent artifacts".
```

     2	name: agent-history-hygiene
     3	description: Commit SpecStory chat transcripts (`.specstory/history/*.md`), Claude Code plan files (`.claude/plans/*.md`, `plansDirectory`), and other coding-agent artifacts (`.cursor/plans/`, `.cursor/rules/`, `.opencode/plans/`, `.specify/`, `.codex/`) alongside the feature diff they produced — without leaking `.env` contents, API keys, or private-key PEM blocks into git history. Use when the user says "commit my chat", "save this specstory session", "stage the plan file", "scrub the transcript", "my .env leaked in chat", "bootstrap pre-commit for this project", or when you notice untracked `.specstory/history/*.md` or `.claude/plans/*.md` files while running `git status`. Also use after an accidental push of a secret to enforce rotate-first, rewrite-last remediation instead of reflexive `git push --force`.
     4	---
     5	
     6	# agent-history-hygiene
     7	
     8	Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
     9	code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
    10	`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.
    11	
    12	Three surfaces, separated by purpose:
    13	
    14	| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
    15	|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
    16	| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
    17	| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
    18	| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
    19	| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
    20	| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |
    21	
    22	## Core invariants
    23	
    24	1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
    25	   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
    26	   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.

     1	"""Golden-corpus tests: stage each fixture in a throwaway git repo, run
     2	`gitleaks git --staged` against `assets/gitleaks.toml.template`, and
     3	assert the expected finding count.
     4	
     5	These catch regressions in:
     6	- allowlist semantics (e.g. defaulting to OR instead of AND)
     7	- config-file compatibility (e.g. mixing `[allowlist]` with `[[allowlists]]`)
     8	- path-scoped allowlist paths drifting away from the real artifact dirs
     9	
    10	If gitleaks is not installed, the whole file skips.
    11	"""
    12	from __future__ import annotations
    13	
    14	import json
    15	import shutil
    16	import subprocess
    17	from pathlib import Path
    18	
    19	import pytest
    20	
    21	pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
    22	    shutil.which("gitleaks") is None,
    23	    reason="gitleaks binary not on PATH",
    24	)
    25	
    26	
    27	def _stage_fixture_at(repo: Path, fixture_path: Path, dest_rel: str) -> None:
    28	    """Copy `fixture_path` to `repo/dest_rel` and git-add it."""
    29	    dest = repo / dest_rel
    30	    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    31	    shutil.copy(fixture_path, dest)
    32	    subprocess.run(["git", "add", "--", dest_rel], cwd=repo, check=True)
    33	
    34	
    35	def _run_gitleaks_staged(repo: Path) -> list[dict]:
    36	    """Run `gitleaks git --staged` and return the JSON findings array."""
    37	    report = repo / "_report.json"
    38	    result = subprocess.run(
    39	        [
    40	            "gitleaks",
    41	            "git",
    42	            "--staged",
    43	            "--config",
    44	            ".gitleaks.toml",
    45	            "--report-format",
    46	            "json",
    47	            "--report-path",
    48	            str(report),
    49	            "--exit-code",
    50	            "0",
    51	        ],
    52	        cwd=repo,
    53	        capture_output=True,
    54	        text=True,
    55	    )
    56	    # Non-zero would indicate config error — surface it for debugging.
    57	    assert result.returncode == 0, (
    58	        f"gitleaks failed:\nstdout: {result.stdout}\nstderr: {result.stderr}"
    59	    )
    60	    if not report.exists() or report.stat().st_size == 0:
    61	        return []
    62	    return json.loads(report.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

I have complete evidence to answer all your questions definitively. Here is the report.

## Bottom line (the critical question)

**No — adding a path-scoped `[[allowlists]]` entry for `tests/fixtures/` to `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` would NOT break `test_gitleaks_corpus.py`.** The corpus test never stages files at `tests/fixtures/` paths. It copies fixture *content* into a throwaway repo at unrelated destination paths, and gitleaks matches allowlist `paths` regexes against the staged file's path in that throwaway repo — which is never under `tests/fixtures/`. A `tests/fixtures/` path allowlist would simply never match, so every fixture would keep firing exactly as before.

Separately: the repo already solves the "out of scope" problem a different way — via a root `.gitleaksignore` (fingerprint-based), not via the template. Details below.

---

## 1. `tests/test_gitleaks_corpus.py`

**Stage actual file vs. copy content into throwaway repo:** It **copies content into a throwaway repo at a different path.** The helper `_stage_fixture_at` does `shutil.copy(fixture_path, dest)` then `git add` the *dest* (`test_gitleaks_corpus.py:27-32`):

--- pitfalls/deploy-pages-times-out-polling-status.md ---
# `actions/deploy-pages` hangs polling for deployment status and times out

## Symptom

A `Docs` workflow that normally finishes in ~30 seconds instead runs for
10 minutes and fails at the deploy step:

```
Run actions/deploy-pages@v5
Getting Pages deployment status...
Current status:
Getting Pages deployment status...
Current status:
...
(repeats for 10 minutes)
##[error]Timeout reached, aborting!
Canceling Pages deployment...
Canceled deployment with ID <sha>
```

Key signal: `Current status:` is followed by **nothing** — the Pages
API is returning an empty status string, not a real state like
`in_progress` / `succeed`. The `build` job itself succeeded and the
artifact uploaded fine; only `deploy-pages` is stuck.

`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pages` afterwards shows `"status": null`
because the stuck deployment got canceled.

## Root cause

GitHub Pages backend transient failure. The deploy action polls
`/pages/deployment/status` until it sees a terminal state; when the
Pages service is degraded, the endpoint returns an empty body and the
poll loop just burns through the 10-minute default timeout.

Nothing in the repo configuration causes this. Adjacent commits on
the same workflow build + deploy cleanly in ~30 seconds both before
and after the incident.

## Workaround

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# test_scan_staged.sh — exit-code contract for scripts/scan-staged.sh.
3	#
4	# Asserts the documented exit codes:
5	#   0   clean
6	#   20  leaks found
7	#   30  gitleaks binary missing
8	#    2  not inside a git repo
9	#
10	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
11	
12	set -u  # intentionally NOT -e: we capture non-zero exit codes
13	
14	TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
15	SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/.." && pwd)"
16	SCAN="$SKILL_DIR/scripts/scan-staged.sh"
17	FIXTURES="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures"
18	
19	# State (no associative arrays — bash 3.2 compat)
20	PASS_COUNT=0
21	FAIL_COUNT=0
22	FAIL_LOG=""
23	
24	red()   { printf '\033[31m%s\033[0m' "$*"; }
25	green() { printf '\033[32m%s\033[0m' "$*"; }
26	dim()   { printf '\033[2m%s\033[0m' "$*"; }
27	
28	pass() {
29	  PASS_COUNT=$((PASS_COUNT + 1))
30	  printf '  %s %s\n' "$(green PASS)" "$1"
31	}
32	fail() {
33	  FAIL_COUNT=$((FAIL_COUNT + 1))
34	  printf '  %s %s\n' "$(red FAIL)" "$1"
35	  FAIL_LOG="${FAIL_LOG}FAIL: $1\n"
36	}
37	
38	# make_repo — spin up an isolated tmp repo with an initial commit.
39	# Prints the path to stdout.
40	make_repo() {
41	  local d
42	  d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/test-scan-staged.XXXXXX)
43	  git -C "$d" init -q -b main
44	  git -C "$d" -c user.email=test@example.com -c user.name=test \
45	      commit -q --allow-empty -m init
46	  printf '%s' "$d"
47	}
48	
49	# Copy fixture + stage it under the given relative path.
50	stage_fixture() {
51	  local repo="$1" fixture="$2" dest_rel="$3"
52	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$repo/$dest_rel")"
53	  cp "$FIXTURES/$fixture" "$repo/$dest_rel"
54	  git -C "$repo" add -- "$dest_rel"
55	}
56	
57	if ! command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
58	  printf '%s gitleaks binary missing\n' "$(dim SKIP)"
59	  printf '  (skipping positive cases; running the exit-30 contract only)\n\n'
60	  GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE=0
61	else
62	  GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE=1
63	fi
64	
65	printf '== scan-staged exit-code contract ==\n\n'
66	
67	# --- Case 1: clean file → exit 0 ---
68	if [ "$GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE" = "1" ]; then
69	  REPO=$(make_repo)
70	  # Install the gitleaks config so rules apply.
71	  cp "$SKILL_DIR/assets/gitleaks.toml.template" "$REPO/.gitleaks.toml"
72	  stage_fixture "$REPO" "clean.md" "notes.md"
73	  (cd "$REPO" && bash "$SCAN" >/dev/null 2>&1)
74	  rc=$?
75	  if [ "$rc" = "0" ]; then pass "clean fixture → exit 0"
76	  else fail "clean fixture → exit 0 (got $rc)"
77	  fi
78	  rm -rf "$REPO"
79	fi
80	
81	# --- Case 2: real leak inside .claude/plans/ → exit 20 ---
82	if [ "$GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE" = "1" ]; then
83	  REPO=$(make_repo)
84	  cp "$SKILL_DIR/assets/gitleaks.toml.template" "$REPO/.gitleaks.toml"
85	  stage_fixture "$REPO" "real_anthropic.md" ".claude/plans/p1.md"
86	  (cd "$REPO" && bash "$SCAN" >/dev/null 2>&1)

89	  else fail "real Anthropic key → exit 20 (got $rc)"
90	  fi
91	  rm -rf "$REPO"
92	fi
93	
94	# --- Case 3: not in a git repo → exit 2 ---
95	OUTSIDE=$(mktemp -d /tmp/test-scan-outside.XXXXXX)
96	(cd "$OUTSIDE" && bash "$SCAN" >/dev/null 2>&1)
97	rc=$?
98	if [ "$rc" = "2" ]; then pass "outside git repo → exit 2"
99	else fail "outside git repo → exit 2 (got $rc)"
100	fi
101	rm -rf "$OUTSIDE"
102	
103	# --- Case 4: gitleaks missing → exit 30 ---
104	# Simulate by running with an empty PATH so `command -v gitleaks` fails.
105	REPO=$(make_repo)
106	cp "$SKILL_DIR/assets/gitleaks.toml.template" "$REPO/.gitleaks.toml" 2>/dev/null || true
107	# Keep /bin and /usr/bin so the script itself (bash, git, mktemp) runs.

110	rc=$?
111	if [ "$rc" = "30" ]; then pass "no gitleaks on PATH → exit 30"
112	else fail "no gitleaks on PATH → exit 30 (got $rc)"
113	fi
114	rm -rf "$REPO"
115	
116	# --- Case 5: empty JSON report `[]` handled as clean → exit 0 ---
117	# This is the regression we caught during initial verification: gitleaks
118	# writes `[]` for zero findings; scan-staged.sh must not treat that as

120	if [ "$GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE" = "1" ]; then

128	  fi

130	fi

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scan-staged.sh — run gitleaks on the current staged diff with
3	# agent-friendly exit codes.
4	#
5	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
6	
7	set -euo pipefail
8	
9	usage() {
10	  cat <<'EOF'
11	Usage: scan-staged.sh [OPTIONS]
12	
13	Scan the staged diff for secrets using `gitleaks git --staged`. Intended
14	as the "last line of defense" wrapper agents call before `git commit` so
15	they can branch on structured exit codes.
16	
17	Options:
18	  --redact           Pass --redact to gitleaks (default: off; findings
19	                     print the literal secret for debugging).
20	  --no-redact        Explicit opt-out of --redact (overrides --redact).
21	  --config PATH      Path to .gitleaks.toml (default: repo root if present).
22	  --verbose          Print gitleaks' own output to stderr.
23	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
24	
25	Output (stdout):
26	  - If clean: no output.
27	  - If leaks found: one JSON object per line with the finding details.
28	
29	Exit codes:
30	  0   clean — no secrets found
31	  10  leaks found (and redacted if --redact was passed)
32	  20  leaks found, not redacted (caller must rotate + re-stage)
33	  30  gitleaks binary not installed
34	  40  gitleaks error (bad config, unreadable repo, etc.)
35	  1   invalid arguments
36	  2   not inside a git repo
37	EOF
38	}
39	
40	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
41	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
42	
43	REDACT=0
44	CONFIG=""
45	VERBOSE=0
46	
47	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
48	  case "$1" in
49	    --redact)     REDACT=1; shift ;;
50	    --no-redact)  REDACT=0; shift ;;
51	    --config)     CONFIG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
52	    --config=*)   CONFIG="${1#--config=}"; shift ;;
53	    --verbose)    VERBOSE=1; shift ;;
54	    --help|-h)    usage; exit 0 ;;
55	    -*)           die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
56	    *)            die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
57	  esac
58	done
59	
60	# Check prerequisites.
61	if ! command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
62	  log "gitleaks not installed. Install hints:"
63	  log "  macOS:   brew install gitleaks"
64	  log "  Linux:   https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases"
65	  exit 30
66	fi
67	
68	if ! git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
69	  die "not inside a git repo" 2
70	fi
71	cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
72	
73	# Auto-discover config if not specified.
74	if [ -z "$CONFIG" ] && [ -f ".gitleaks.toml" ]; then
75	  CONFIG=".gitleaks.toml"
76	fi
77	
78	report_path="$(mktemp -t gitleaks-report.XXXXXX.json)"
79	trap 'rm -f "$report_path"' EXIT
80	
81	# Assemble the command. Post v8.19.0 `gitleaks git --staged` replaces the
82	# deprecated `gitleaks protect --staged`.
83	cmd=(gitleaks git --staged
84	     --report-format json
85	     --report-path "$report_path"
86	     --exit-code 0)
87	[ -n "$CONFIG" ] && cmd+=(--config "$CONFIG")
88	[ "$REDACT" = "1" ] && cmd+=(--redact)
89	
90	# Capture gitleaks' own exit code — with `--exit-code 0` it returns 0
91	# whether leaks are found or not, so a non-zero exit means the tool itself
92	# failed (config error, unreadable repo, etc.).
93	stderr_capture="$(mktemp -t gitleaks-stderr.XXXXXX)"
94	trap 'rm -f "$report_path" "$stderr_capture"' EXIT
95	
96	gl_rc=0
97	if [ "$VERBOSE" = "1" ]; then
98	  "${cmd[@]}" >&2 2>>"$stderr_capture" || gl_rc=$?
99	else
100	  "${cmd[@]}" >/dev/null 2>"$stderr_capture" || gl_rc=$?
101	fi
102	
103	if [ "$gl_rc" -ne 0 ]; then
104	  log "gitleaks failed to run (exit $gl_rc). Tail of its stderr:"
105	  tail -n 20 "$stderr_capture" >&2 || true
106	  exit 40
107	fi
108	
109	# Gitleaks writes an empty file when truly clean, or `[]` when the report
110	# format is JSON and there are zero findings. Normalize both to "clean".
111	if [ ! -s "$report_path" ]; then
112	  exit 0
113	fi
114	
115	finding_count=0
116	if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
117	  finding_count=$(python3 - "$report_path" <<'PY'
118	import json, sys
119	try:
120	    with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as f:
121	        data = json.load(f)
122	except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
123	    print(0)
124	    sys.exit(0)
125	print(len(data) if isinstance(data, list) else 0)
126	PY
127	)
128	else
129	  # Fallback: grep for a non-empty array. `[]` → 0, anything else → non-zero.
130	  case "$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$report_path")" in
131	    ""|"[]") finding_count=0 ;;
132	    *)        finding_count=1 ;;
133	  esac
134	fi
135	
136	if [ "$finding_count" -eq 0 ]; then
137	  exit 0
138	fi
139	
140	# Re-emit each finding as its own JSON object (one per line) for ergonomic
141	# agent consumption. Findings file is a JSON *array*; slice it into lines
142	# using python3 — avoid adding a jq dependency.
143	if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
144	  python3 - "$report_path" <<'PY'
145	import json, sys
146	with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as f:
147	    data = json.load(f)
148	for finding in data:
149	    # Keep only the most useful fields; caller can re-open the raw report.
150	    slim = {
151	        "rule_id": finding.get("RuleID"),
152	        "file": finding.get("File"),
153	        "line": finding.get("StartLine"),
154	        "commit": finding.get("Commit") or "STAGED",
155	        "match": finding.get("Match"),
156	    }
157	    print(json.dumps(slim, ensure_ascii=False))
158	PY
159	else
160	  # Fallback: dump the raw array.
161	  cat "$report_path"
162	fi
163	
164	if [ "$REDACT" = "1" ]; then
165	  log "gitleaks found leaks AND --redact was passed."
166	  log "  NOTE: gitleaks --redact only masks the CLI output, it does NOT"
167	  log "        rewrite files. Use redact_secrets.py --fix (or the pre-commit"
168	  log "        redact-agent-secrets hook) to actually scrub the artifacts."
169	  exit 10
170	else
171	  log "gitleaks found leaks. See JSON findings on stdout."
172	  log "Next: rotate the secret at the provider, then run redact_secrets.py --fix,"
173	  log "      then re-stage and re-run this check. DO NOT \`git push --force\`."
174	  exit 20
175	fi
176
```

1	# Tests for agent-history-hygiene
2	
3	Run the full suite:

5	```bash

9	# Or directly
10	uv run --extra dev pytest skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/tests/ -q
11	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/tests/test_scan_staged.sh
12	```
13	
14	## Layout
15	
16	- `fixtures/` — paired `.md` files exercising gitleaks rules + allowlist.
17	  Each filename encodes its expected behavior (e.g. `real_anthropic.md`
18	  should fire, `example_shapes.md` should be allowlisted when staged
19	  inside an agent-artifact directory).

21	  `assets/redact_secrets.py` as an importable module.

2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

5	## Project Overview
6	
7	A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills`. Contains custom-authored skills (`skills/local/`) and cherry-picked 3rd-party skills (`skills/vendor/`) synced from upstream repos.

The nested `local/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).

12

15	make sync
16	
17	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)

19	
20	# Validate and render the repo backlog board

22

24	# that drives the grouped install UI of `npx skills add ...`).

26

29	./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path/to/skill
30	# Group under a series subdir (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/)

32	
33	# Add a structured TODO entry (preferred over editing TODO.md by hand)

36

39	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh --batch     # only formalize parseable key=value lines
40

42	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<shipped summary>"
43

53	## Vendor System
54	
55	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
56	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
57	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
58	
59	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA.
60	
61	Active series in this repo:
62	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
63	
64	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
65	
66	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
67	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
68	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
69	
70	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
71	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
72	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
73	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
74	  the `npx skills` CLI has no lockfile, so users who installed the old
75	  name won't auto-map on `npx skills update`.
76	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
77	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
78	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
79	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
80	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
81	
82	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
83	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
84	
85	## Marketplace Catalog
86	
87	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
88	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
89	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
90	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
91	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
92	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
93	for the full mechanism.
94	
95	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
96	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
97	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
98	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
99	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
100	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
101	
102	## SKILL.md Format
103	
104	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
105	
106	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
107	
108	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
109	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
110	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
111	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
112	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
113	
114	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
115	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
116	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
117	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
118	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
119	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
120	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
121	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
122	
123	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
124	
125	```bash
126	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
127	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
128	
129	# …or remove them afterward
130	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
131	```
132	
133	## Project Memory Workflow
134	
135	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
136	
137	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
138	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
139	
140	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
141	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
142	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
143	
144	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
145	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
146	
147	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
148	
149	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
150	
151	   ```bash
152	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
153	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
154	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
155	   ```
156	
157	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
158	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
159	
160	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
161	
162	   ```bash
163	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
164	   ```
165	
166	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
167	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
168	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
169	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
170	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
171	
172	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
173	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
174	   afterwards to catch drift.
175	
176	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
177	
178	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
179	
180	```bash
181	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
182	```
183	
184	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
185	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
186	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
187	
188	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
189	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
190	
191	### External skill / MCP / domain catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
192	
193	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
194	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
195	own conventions). It has three subareas:
196	
197	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
198	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
199	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
200	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
201	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
202	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
203	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
204	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
205	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
206	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
207	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
208	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
209	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
210	  status / license / last_verified`).
211	
212	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
213	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
214	
215	| Status | Meaning |
216	|---|---|
217	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
218	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
219	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
220	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
221	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
222	
223	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
224	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
225	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
226	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
227	
228	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
229	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
230	
231	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
232	
233	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
234	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
235	
236	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
237	2. The root cause
238	3. The workaround
239	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
240	
241	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
242	the explanation they do not know yet.

2	
3	Past traps we have already debugged. This is a symptoms-first knowledge base:

```text
1	# Screenshot from `.evidence/` renders as a broken image in a PR comment
2	
3	## Symptom
4	
5	An agent captures a demo screenshot with the `demo-evidence` skill, then
6	tries to show it in a pull-request comment by linking the file:
7	
8	```markdown
9	![login demo](.evidence/claude-5f932f43/2026-…-login/login.png)
10	```
11	
12	The image renders as a **broken-image icon** (or GitHub silently drops it).
13	The same is true for a raw URL to the file on the branch — GitHub returns
14	404, because the path was never pushed.
15	
16	## Root cause
17	
18	`demo-evidence` files bundles under `.evidence/`, which `new-bundle.sh`
19	adds to `.gitignore` **by design** (acceptance artifacts should never enter
20	git history). A gitignored file is:
21	
22	- not committed, so there is no `raw.githubusercontent.com/<branch>/…` URL, and
23	- not part of the PR diff, so GitHub's Markdown image proxy (Camo) has
24	  nothing to fetch.
25	
26	GitHub only inlines images from a public HTTPS URL or from a file the user
27	drag-drops into the comment box (which uploads to
28	`user-images.githubusercontent.com`). A local, gitignored path is neither.
29	
30	## Workaround
31	
32	The evidence bundle is meant to be reviewed **locally**, not embedded in a
33	PR. Pick one:
34	
35	- **Local review (intended path):** point the reviewer at
36	  `<bundle>/MANIFEST.md`; they open it on a checkout of the branch.
37	- **Manual embed:** drag-drop the PNG into the PR comment box so GitHub
38	  uploads it to its own CDN, then paste the generated URL.
39	- **Out-of-band:** upload the media to any public HTTPS host (gist raw URL
40	  for images, a CDN/release asset for video) and reference that URL.
41	
42	## Prevention / invariant
43	
44	**Gitignored evidence has no public URL — never link a `.evidence/` path in a
45	PR/issue and expect it to render.** Automated PR posting that embeds media
46	must first publish the file to a durable URL, and must run a secret scan
47	first (screenshots/logs can leak). That capability is deliberately deferred:
48	see the `TODO P?` item *"demo-evidence: PR posting for evidence bundles"*.
49	For v1, treat `.evidence/` as a local-only acceptance surface.
50
```
</details></tool-use>

2	
3	A `pitfalls/` directory captures non-obvious traps you've already debugged

5	straight to the fix.
6	
7	This page documents the format used by

12	
13	```
14	pitfalls/
15	├── README.md                              # index + cross-reference table
16	├── <symptom-slug-1>.md                    # one trap per file
17	├── <symptom-slug-2>.md
18	└── …
19	```
20	
21	The slug is the **symptom**, not the root cause. You search by what you
22	see in the error, not by the explanation you eventually learned.
23	
24	## Single pitfall doc — required sections
25	
26	Each `pitfalls/<slug>.md` should answer four questions in this order:
27	
28	1. **Symptom** — the verbatim error text or behavior. Copy-paste, don't
29	   paraphrase. Paraphrasing kills `grep`.
30	2. **Root cause** — the underlying mechanism, in one or two paragraphs.
31	3. **Workaround** — exact steps to recover. Code blocks where applicable.
32	4. **Prevention** — the invariant that, if applied, would have prevented
33	   the trap. If the prevention is severe enough (silent corruption,
34	   cross-machine recurrence), graduate it to a Hard invariant in
35	   `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` and link both ways.
36	
37	The full template lives at
38	[`skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/assets/pitfall-doc.md.template`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/assets/pitfall-doc.md.template).
39	
40	## Title / slug guidance
41	
42	Write the title the way the search query would look:
43	
44	| ✅ Symptom-first | ❌ Root-cause-first |
45	|---|---|
46	| `gh-api-404-on-tree-endpoint.md` | `vendor-yaml-branch-handling.md` |
47	| `npx-skills-empty-after-install.md` | `skills-discovery-depth-fallback.md` |
48	| `mkdocs-strict-fails-on-relative-md.md` | `mkdocs-link-validation-rules.md` |
49	
50	The agent reading the pitfall is asking *"is this what just happened to
51	me?"* — the title needs to match the question, not the answer.
52	
53	## When NOT to use `pitfalls/`
54	
55	- **Project-specific bugs that are already fixed.** Use `git log` /
56	  CHANGELOG instead. Pitfalls are for traps that can recur.
57	- **Onboarding gaps.** That's documentation; put it in `docs/` or the
58	  README.
59	- **Generic "things to watch out for" lists.** Without a specific symptom,
60	  there's nothing to grep, so the pitfall doesn't earn its keep.
61	
62	## Cross-referencing
63	
64	`pitfalls/README.md` should keep a small table of pitfalls that live
65	*outside* the directory — for example, a known trap explained inside a
66	specific design doc. The table lets future agents grep the symptom
67	keyword from one place even when the explanation lives elsewhere.
68
```
</details></tool-use>
